title: Ball Wide Mouth Glass Mason Jars with Lids and Bands, Used for Canning, Pickling, Juice, Jam, Jelly, Quart Size 32 Ounce (Pack of 2)
description:
About this item
Versatile glass Mason jars for canning and crafting
Includes Two 32oz Wide Mouth jars with lids and bands
Ideal for creative preserving and storing
Great for gifting and crafting
BPA-free, Made in USA
You may notice that the manufacturer markings made on the jar’s sides end with “24 oz”. The rest of the space between the end of the marking scale and the lid amounts to 8 oz. reviews_5s:
Delivered today separately, bubble wrapped, and then sealed together in a bag, so they don't bump into each other during shipping and break, well done!

Perfect size for making a pitcher of tea or whatever your delight, it's actually a square round, unlike regular mason jars are usually round. I bought the" metal" pour spout tops to convert the jar into a picture. I want to avoid plastics where I can because I find it sometimes alters the flavors of my food and stainless steel and glass are considered the most food-safe materials for food storage and cooking. The only thing is because it is square the lid handle does necessarily line up with the flat side with the designs because the threading on the jar dictates the positioning of where it tighens at and I'm assuming that is true with all the pour spouts given the jar is square not round only the to and botton are. The price for two Mason jars was reasonable given they are a staple in the canning world and you get two, which I like better because you can make up to different drinks, not eating up refrigerated space or awkward to pour from.

I just made my first batch of tea in one of them, pictured below. I also bought the mason infuser filter, which fits and works great, and you can skew the lid on while the infuser is still in the jar, too. This is my recipe; I heated 2 pints of bottled water (half the jar) to a pre-boil stage (about 180 degrees), added 6 tsp/2tbps loose Jasmine green tea into the infuser already in the jar, and poured the hot water into the infuser. I used a chopstick to move the water around the leaves because you only want to steep it for 3 minutes, or you risk the tannins in the tea making your tea bitter. I pulled out the infuser and added another 2 pints of filtered water, which comes to just below the neck of the jar. I use liquid pure Sucralose for my sweeter, and it only took 6 drops to add a touch of sweetness, but not too much. It was easy, healthy, and delicious. I have paid upwards of 5.00 for a 24 oz of green tea when I pick up food out, so I consider this an investment, not to mention homemade is always better. Hibiscus and Fresh raspberry tea are next. I'm set for the summer now.I received these in perfect condition. These are the real deal. TIGHT seal. I use them for EVERYTHING! i. e. , canning, dry food storage, storing leftovers in fridge, drinking glass (get a Koozie with little zipper and handle strap) and sack lunch containers. Who needs a $50 Stanley? Who needs icky plastic boxes. Get these BALL jars - you need them.I have used these small jars to store home made sauces, small quantities of cut veggies, baby to go snacks, and even my in laws hearing aids when she forgot her case. They're water proof, easy to open, and use the universal mason jar lid. They're one of the most multi-functional items in my kitchen.We make a lot of healthy homemade juices and these are perfect. Also great for when I get heavy handed making spaghetti sauce or chicken soup.As it says, they're mason jars. Arrived when they said & were all in good condition.Great product seals good easy to pour liquids intoGood price. No breakage in shipping.I of the 8 was brokenLove these jars. Can’t wait for my first batch of sun tea.Making a starter for sourdough bread
reviews_1s:
It's not that there's any problem with the glass or the lid - it's that the product description says it 6"x6"x6". It isn't. It's 3"x3"x5". Sample size jar for jams or jellies..These things will chip on the lip super easy. If you use them i'd be hesitant in storing food or just make sure you are treating it like it's fine dishware. Check for chips each use. I use these to store leftover food in and one day i saw a chip and panicked, i don't need to be mixing glass in with my food. Especially since i use some for cat food as well.
This isn't my first issue with ball jars. I don't think Ball is a great brand any more. Time to find someone or something else that has the same purpose.The jars are perfect (no problems with breaking or shattering when placed in boiling water.)
A rather pungent smell in the jars and in the bands and lids, so I washed in dishwasher, then took everything out except the jars and parts and ran the dishwasher with no soap (rinse only), sanitize cycle.
Open dishwasher next morning and 40% of the bands had rust spots on the inside of rim! Scraped rust off of four bands, four were ok, and the remaining four were rusted so bad, I threw them away,
Fortunately, I only needed seven half pint jars for my batch of preserves.
I guess I will research and purchase “rust-free bands and lids for Ball/Mason jars”, for my future projects. (One is not supposed to re-use them, anyway.)
It just feels as if the world quality of simple parts has gone away, ehh ? Sheesh!They are not freezer safe! I have now had 8 out of 12 crack which I did not have happen with my older jars. Find another brand if you’re freezing. Or maybe this batch of jars are defective.I will not buy again and many of these jars broke after return window was closed. Most of these jars broke on the bottom of the jar after using them. I have been using Mason Jars for years and this has never happened until now. Maybe it was damaged during transport but the box was not damaged and could not see anything broken before washing and using only once.The glass jars arrived broken and shattered, the glass Ball jars were damaged. I returned the jars and requested a refund. I received a refund for only half of the price I paid. Horrible service!!!!While these jars are affordable, all have a yellow tint to them, leading me to thinking that they’ve been used previously. I wouldn’t have minded if the description had been honest.These jars are not 32 oz.
The lids rust making the jars unusable.
Don’t waste your money!!!Received 8, not 12, off-brand non-Ball jars. Total scam.Someone at Corporate decided that they would package this product with taping the jars together with clear packing tape. We worked for an hour trying to clean the jars with scour pads, even paint thinner. Nothing would remove the glue. When I think Ball jars I think of a clear sanitized jar. It was thin glass, covered with tape glue with a cheap lid. Very disappointing and a sign of the times I guess. We never got the glue off! Too much work and I was embarrassed for a company with such a rich history.
